title: Hotfix: function-call schema mismatch + streaming parse edge with KV-cache on Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ava Chen
description: Multiple customers reported production failures when using function/tool-calling and structured output parsing. Failures span Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC) deployments. Symptoms: intermittent function-call selection errors, truncated function args in structured outputs, and downstream schema validation failures in customer apps. Repro is more common under high-concurrency and when streaming token chunks are used. There is an interaction with the KV cache that causes stale signature selection when requests deduplicate or hit cached prefixes.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12: Initial escalation from Support: two P1 customers (masked) reporting 502s and malformed function payloads during peak traffic. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions with function_call=auto and streaming=true.
2026-03-12: Reproduced locally with scripted load: when chunk boundaries split JSON token sequences, parser accepted partial JSON and emitted a function call event with missing fields.
2026-03-12: Observed path divergence between runtime-parser v1.4 (hosted) and v1.2 (older private appliance images). v1.2 lacks tolerant incremental-JSON reassembly logic introduced in v1.3.

2026-03-12: KV cache interaction: cache hit for prefix-only requests returned inference result tied to a previous function-signature set; downstream router used cached metadata to choose function version, leading to schema mismatch for newly-deployed function signatures.
root_cause: Two related issues: (1) streaming parser accepted incomplete chunk-terminated JSON and emitted partial function-call events; (2) KV cache metadata lacked signature-versioning, so cached responses could be associated with deprecated function schemas. Combined, these caused customers to receive malformed structured outputs or function args that failed schema validation in their code.
temporary_mitigation: Deploy a service-side sanitizer that buffers stream chunks for function-call tokens until a full JSON token boundary is observed (config flag: runtime:stream_buffer_min_ms=40).
Enable an immediate cache-compatibility guard: when function-signature-version != request.desired_signature_version, bypass cache and force recompute.
Advise Support to disable streaming for affected customers as a short-term workaround and route them through a canary with the sanitizer enabled.
Add monitoring dashboard: percent of function-call events with 'partial_chunk' tag and cache-bypass rate.
proposed_fix_summary: 1) Update streaming parser to perform incremental JSON token reassembly and reject/hold incomplete function-call events until the full object completes. 2) Add signature-version metadata to KV cache keys and implement automatic invalidation on function schema change or model rollouts. 3) Add backward-compatible tolerance to structured-output deserializer to accept optional/missing named args when allowed by the function signature policy.
implementation_plan: Implement incremental parser changes in runtime/parser and add unit tests for chunk boundary cases
Add signature-version to cache key formation in runtime/cache and write migration tests
Update router to consult cache metadata and fall back safely
Run full unit+integration test matrix (hosted, dedicated config, private appliance image)
Deploy to dedicated canary pool (small capacity) with feature flag runtime.hotfix_parser_enabled=true
Monitor for 6 hours, then rollout to Hosted API controlled canary; coordinate private appliance images with Solutions for on-prem upgrades
ci_notes: Added 12 new unit tests and 3 integration scenarios. CI must pass linux-x86 gpu and aarch64 smoke tests before canary. Flaky test observed in streaming/split-json-02 (investigating timeouts).
deploy_plan: Canary -> Dedicated (1 pool) -> Hosted API (region-by-region) -> Private appliance image published (upgrade assistant notice). Use rolling restart, kill-switch flag runtime.hotfix_parser_enabled to revert in <10m. Target full rollout by 2026-03-20.

resolution_summary: Parser and cache fixes implemented in runtime-1.22-hotfix2. Initial canary reduced malformed events by ~98%. Full rollout scheduled; private customers will receive appliance images and upgrade guidance. Short-term buffering and cache-guard mitigations reduced immediate customer impact while patch progressed.
